explanation: Eating, passing food, or gesturing with the left hand is considered unclean specifically in Singapore's Malay and Indian communities, since the left hand is traditionally reserved for personal hygiene. In Chinese-majority or Westernized settings (most restaurants, hawker centres, offices), it draws no attention at all since cutlery or chopsticks are used.
local_tip: At a Malay or Indian household, or when eating traditional dishes with your hands, use only your right hand for eating, passing dishes, and giving or receiving items.
regional_note: Strongest in Malay-Muslim and Indian households that eat with their hands; largely irrelevant in Chinese or international dining contexts where cutlery or chopsticks are standard.

also_check.note: Using the left hand for eating or passing food is considered unclean and impolite in most traditional households.
The left hand is reserved for hygiene; eating or passing food with it is a clear faux pas.
There is no left-hand taboo; chopstick etiquette matters far more than which hand you use.
